must_fix: State the terminal damping assumption explicitly. For real E and e_i, η+γ/2>0 makes the proof of invertibility of M go through. Under the listed assumptions η>0 and q_i>0 alone, the unconditional claim is false. Take γ=−2η, m=0, e_s=e_o=E, q_s=q_o=1/2 and orthogonal terminal states in dimension two. Then f_s=q_s and f_o=q_o are nonzero, yet M=0. If transmission carries a separate multiplicative factor involving γ, its nonvanishing is also required for the zero-transmission equivalence.

proof_assessment.determinant_and_conjugation: Taking the displayed R_so factorization as the starting identity, let U=[ψ_s,ψ_o], D=diag(q_s/f_s,q_o/f_o) and G=UᴴC⁻¹U. The determinant lemma gives det(M)/det(C)=det(I−GD), and UᴴM⁻¹U=(I−GD)⁻¹G. In the s,o entry, the two terms involving D_oo G_so G_oo cancel, leaving G_so/det(I−GD). This proves the claimed factor in the stated direction without assuming G is Hermitian or invertible. The imaginary-part proof for C is valid, and it applies to M under the terminal damping condition above.
proof_assessment.sharpness_and_range: For fixed v, the largest overlap of Cv/‖Cv‖ with a unit vector orthogonal to v is its perpendicular projection norm. In the proposed construction u_iᴴv=√t_i, so the perpendicular part of a_i u_i u_iᴴv is exactly |a_i|√(t_i(1−t_i))w. The negative phase in u_i is correct. Thus Cv=αv−βw, and ψ_s=w gives both cancellation and overlap magnitude β/√(|α|²+β²). Since α never vanishes on the compact box, the maximum exists and is strictly below one. Along t=τt_star the overlap is continuous with endpoint values zero and c_star. The intermediate value theorem gives the full interval without requiring monotonicity.
proof_assessment.cone_and_minimax: For fixed r≥0 the disk constraint on (2t_i−1,2u_i) with u_i≥0 is equivalent to 0≤t_i≤1 and 0≤u_i≤√(t_i(1−t_i)). Choosing each upper endpoint proves exactness of the feasibility test, including equality. For the dual, the term −Re(conj(z)α) expands to −Re(z)+Σ_i b_i(z)t_i with the stated sign and conjugation. The objective is continuous, concave in t and affine in z on compact convex domains, so Sion's exchange applies. Substitution x=2t−1 gives the stated scalar maximum (b+√(b²+|a_i|²))/2. Hence F is the pointwise maximum of affine functions of z and is convex.
proof_assessment.closest_point_and_zero_boundary: Let H(r)=max_t[β−r|α|]=min_{|z|≤r}F(z). Since min_t|α|>0 and β/|α| attains its maximum, H(r)>0 for 0≤r<r_star, H(r_star)=0, and H(r)<0 for r>r_star. The disk minimum is attained by continuity. The disk of radius r_star therefore contains a point with F=0, and every smaller disk misses {F≤0}. This proves the proposed minimum-norm formula with attainment.
proof_assessment.edge_cases: For m=1 the squared turning sine simplifies to |a|²t(1−t)/[1+(d0²−1)t], where d0=|1−a|>0. Its derivative has the sign of [1−(1+d0)t][1+(d0−1)t], giving t_star=1/(1+d0) and c_star=|a|/(1+d0), including d0=1. For m=0, α=1, β=0 and F(z)=−Re(z). The closest feasible point is z=0, so r_star=c_star=0.

response.conditioning_or_robustness_limits: At fixed coefficients with positive damping and nonzero transmission prefactors, a strict overlap margin c≥c_star+δ on a nonempty set gives a positive minimum transmission by compactness and continuity. The proof supplies no numerical size for that minimum relative to ε. The determinant ratio and endpoint prefactors matter for that comparison. At or below c_star the witness establishes attainability only with freely chosen state directions. Above c_star the impossibility transfers to every restricted family with the same coefficients.

universal_cap.finding: The sharp inequality c_star ≤ ρ/√(ρ²+4η²) holds for every allowed partition of the context mass and every choice of real onsite values. Equality is attainable when the onsite values and state directions are free.
universal_cap.weighted_inequalities: Write s_i = u_i²+η². Then y/η = Σ q_i t_i/s_i. For β, apply Cauchy–Schwarz to the factors √(q_i(1−t_i)) and √(q_i t_i/s_i), giving β² ≤ (ρ−p)y/η. For 1−α, apply complex Cauchy–Schwarz to Σ q_i t_i/(u_i+iη), giving |1−α|² ≤ p y/η. Adding and using the stated completed square gives β² ≤ (ρ/(2η))²|α|².
universal_cap.sharpness: For ρ>0, take every u_i=ρ/2, every t_i=1/2 and all context states equal to the stated common-plane vector. The aggregate coefficient is a=ρ/(ρ/2+iη), independent of the mass partition. Since |1−a|=1, C preserves norms. For the constructed v and w, |wᴴCv|=|a|/2 equals the cap, while wᴴC⁻¹(Cv)=0 gives exact cancellation.
universal_cap.onsite_range_and_edges: At E=0, each attaining onsite value satisfies −ρ/2 < e_i=q_i−ρ/2 ≤ ρ/2. A single context token reaches the upper endpoint. Positive terminal masses imply ρ<1, so the entire interval lies strictly inside (−1,1). For ρ=0 the cap is zero. The rearranged mass requirement applies for 0<c<1. At c=1, exact cancellation is impossible for every finite ρ and η>0.

finite_bound.finding: The proposed lower bound holds with the stated fourth power.
finite_bound.angle_and_projection: The substitution v ↦ Cv/‖Cv‖ is a bijection on unit vectors and exchanges the two directions in the projective angle for C and C⁻¹. The optional bound Σ|a_i| also holds because the distance from unit v to span(Cv) is at most ‖v−Cv‖. For ŷ=C⁻¹ψ_o/‖C⁻¹ψ_o‖, decompose ψ_s and ŷ along ψ_o and its orthogonal complement. The reverse triangle inequality gives |ψ_sᴴŷ| ≥ max(0,c√(1−b²)−√(1−c²)b), including for complex states.
finite_bound.norms: ‖C‖ ≤ K0 gives ‖C⁻¹ψ_o‖ ≥ 1/K0. With X having context columns √q_i ψ_i and A=diag(u_i+iη)−XᴴX, Woodbury gives C⁻¹=I+XA⁻¹Xᴴ. Since Im(vᴴAv)=η‖v‖², ‖A⁻¹‖ ≤ 1/η. Together with ‖X‖² ≤ ρ this proves K1.
finite_bound.determinant_and_edges: For U=[ψ_s,ψ_o], the Gram matrix gives ‖U‖²=1+c, including c=1. Put L=1+(1+c)K1 dmax. Each singular value of the two-by-two terminal correction matrix is at most L, so |D| ≤ L². Its determinant is nonzero by invertibility of C and M. Squaring the amplitude gives L⁴ in the transmission denominator. With empty context, C=I and K0=K1=1. For c≤b the lower bound is zero.
